title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
summary: Guanciale, egg, Pecorino and black pepper, and no cream. The sauce is an emulsion made off the heat, so the whole trick is having everything ready before the pasta is.
equipment: Mixing bowl and a fork or whisk

items.note: or pancetta; rind off, cut into 1 cm batons

mise.title: Get the water on
mise.text: Fill the large pot with 3 litres of water, cover it, and set it over high heat. Less water than usual means starchier pasta water, which helps the sauce come together.

mise.title: Toast and crack the pepper
mise.text: Toast 2 tsp peppercorns in the dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about a minute. Tip them out and crack them coarsely in a mortar or under the flat of a knife.
mise.tip: Wipe the skillet out afterwards. You'll render the guanciale in it.

mise.title: Cut the guanciale
mise.text: Trim off the rind. Slice the guanciale 1 cm thick, then cut the slices into 1 cm batons. You want about 150 g.

mise.title: Grate the cheese
mise.text: Finely grate 80 g Pecorino Romano on the Microplane. Set aside 20 g in a small bowl for serving.
mise.tip: Fine and fluffy melts. Coarse shreds clump.

mise.title: Make the egg paste
mise.text: In the mixing bowl, beat 4 yolks and 1 whole egg with the remaining 60 g Pecorino and most of the cracked pepper. It should be a thick, sticky paste.
mise.tip: Save the egg whites for an omelette or meringue.

mise.title: Set out the tools
mise.text: Put the tongs and the mug by the stove, and warm the bowls if you like. From here on, things move fast.

steps.title: Salt the water
steps.text: When the water is at a rolling boil, add 1 tbsp kosher salt. That's less than you'd usually use, because the Pecorino and guanciale are both salty.

steps.title: Render the guanciale
steps.text: Put the guanciale in the cold skillet and set it over medium-low heat. Let the fat render slowly, stirring now and then, until the edges are golden and crisp but the centres are still chewy.
steps.tip: Starting cold renders more fat. Keep this timer running and go to the next step.

steps.title: Drop the pasta
steps.text: While the guanciale renders, add the spaghetti to the boiling water and stir for the first minute so it doesn't stick. Cook it for 2 minutes less than the package says. It finishes in the pan.

steps.title: Take the pan off the heat
steps.text: When the guanciale is done, turn off the heat and move the skillet off the burner. Leave the guanciale and all its fat in the pan.
steps.tip: A pan that's too hot scrambles the eggs. Off the heat is the whole technique.

steps.title: Loosen the egg
steps.text: Just before the pasta is ready, whisk 2 to 3 tablespoons of the hot pasta water into the egg paste. Then fill the mug with more pasta water and keep it by the stove.

steps.title: Toss the pasta in the fat
steps.text: Use the tongs to move the pasta straight into the skillet, letting a little water come with it. Toss it in the fat for about 30 seconds to coat it and cool the pan slightly.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Pour the egg mixture over the pasta and toss constantly, adding splashes of pasta water, until it turns creamy and glossy and coats every strand.
steps.tip: Too thin? Set the pan back over the lowest heat for a few seconds while you toss. Too thick? Add more water. Never let it bubble.

steps.title: Serve right away
steps.text: Twirl the pasta into the bowls and top it with the reserved Pecorino and the rest of the pepper. Carbonara waits for no one.

notes: No cream, garlic or onion in the Roman version. The creaminess comes from egg, cheese and starchy water.
Pancetta works if you can't find guanciale. Thick-cut unsmoked bacon is the last resort.
